Asymptotic Variance–Covariance of the Transition Probability Vector

Source: R/03_p.R
vcov_p.Rd

Constructs the block-diagonal asymptotic variance–covariance matrix for the row-wise vectorization of an empirical transition matrix from an irreducible finite-state Markov chain.

Usage

vcov_p(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'MarkovChain'
vcov_p(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'StochMat'
vcov_p(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
vcov_p(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A MarkovChain or StochMat object representing an \(s \times s\) row-stochastic transition matrix. The Markov chain must be irreducible.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

Value

A numeric block-diagonal matrix of dimension \(s^2 \times s^2\), where \(s\) is the number of states.

Details

Let \(\widehat{\mathbf P}(n)\) be the empirical transition matrix estimated from a trajectory of length \(n\), and let \(\widehat{\mathbf p}(n)\) be its row-wise vectorization. Under irreducibility, the empirical transition matrix is strongly consistent and asymptotically normal: $$ \sqrt{n} \left\{ \widehat{\mathbf p}(n) - \mathbf p \right\} \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{d} \mathbf W_{\mathbf p}, \qquad \mathbf W_{\mathbf p} \sim \mathcal N_{s^2} \left( \mathbf 0_{s^2}, \Sigma_{\mathbf p} \right). $$

This function calculates the matrix \(\Sigma_{\mathbf p}\). Specifically, if \(\boldsymbol{\pi} = (\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_s)^{\mathsf T}\) is the unique stationary distribution, then the asymptotic covariance matrix is $$ \Sigma_{\mathbf p} = \begin{pmatrix} \pi_1^{-1}\Lambda_1 & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & \pi_2^{-1}\Lambda_2 & \cdots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \cdots & \pi_s^{-1}\Lambda_s \end{pmatrix}, $$

where $$ \Lambda_i = \operatorname{diag}(p_{i\bullet}) - p_{i\bullet}p_{i\bullet}^{\mathsf T}, \qquad i = 1,\ldots,s. $$

References

Gavrilopoulos, G., Trevezas, S., and Votsi, I. (2026). Matrix asymptotic calculus for plug-in maximum likelihood estimators in finite Markov chains. arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.17161. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17161. See Theorem 1 for the row-wise transition covariance.

Sadek, A., and Limnios, N. (2002). Asymptotic properties for maximum likelihood estimators for reliability and failure rates of Markov chains. Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods, 31(10), 1837–1861. doi:10.1081/STA-120014916 . See Proposition 1 (p. 1846) for the asymptotic covariance matrix of the transition probabilities.

Examples

P <- StochMat(matrix(c(0.8, 0.2, 0.3, 0.7), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))
Sigma <- vcov_p(P)
dim(Sigma) # Four transition probabilities in row-wise order
#> [1] 4 4
